item.title: OpenTelemetry plugin enables comprehensive tracing and metrics for Hermes Agent
item.description:
OpenTelemetry plugin enables comprehensive tracing and metrics for Hermes Agent

An OpenTelemetry plugin has been released for Hermes Agent, enabling detailed observability for AI agent workflows. This update allows every interaction and process within the agent to be tracked and exported to compatible backends.

🔍 Overview

The plugin integrates Hermes Agent with OpenTelemetry (OTel) standards. It captures various operational aspects of the agent, including:

  • Model calls and API requests
  • Tool calls and skill loads
  • Approvals and delegated sub-agents

All of these events are structured into a single OTel trace for each Hermes turn. This trace includes metrics for tokens, costs, and latency. Optionally, logs and structured events are also captured and exported to any OTLP backend via HTTP or gRPC.

🧩 How it works

The plugin uses a comprehensive attribute schema to log details across different components of the agent. Attributes are emitted in two conventions to support various backends:

  • OpenInference (llm.*, input.value): Optimized for Phoenix.
  • OTel GenAI (gen_ai.*): Optimized for Langfuse, Weave, and generic dashboards.

This dual-convention approach eliminates the need for custom mapping in backend configurations.

⚙️ Key details

Specific trace data includes:

Component Tracked Details
Skills Name, source (skill_view / path read), path; remains open until the turn ends
Model Calls Model, provider, input user message, output assistant response
Metrics Token counts (incl. cache and reasoning buckets), duration, finish reason, request parameters
Errors ERROR status, exception details, and retry metadata
Tool Calls Arguments, results, inferred target/command, and hermes.tool.outcome (completed, error, timeout, blocked, cancelled)
Approvals Decision wait time, choice (once, session, always, deny, timeout, smart_approve, smart_deny, smart_escalate), and who decided
Sub-agents Role, goal, status, duration, summary, child’s model, and total subtree cost
Kanban A card’s run is traced from the dispatcher’s claim through the worker’s turn

The hermes.query_source attribute distinguishes the origin of calls:

  • main: The agent loop’s own calls
  • subagent: A delegated child’s calls
  • auxiliary: Calls made on the agent’s behalf (e.g., titling, compression, Mixture-of-Agents references, vision). These are tagged with hermes.auxiliary.task.

For successful git commit operations, the plugin records hermes.tool.git_commit, which is also counted as a hermes.commit.count and a commit event.

🚀 Multi-agent Support

The plugin supports complex orchestration patterns:

  • Delegated children
  • Kanban workers operating on different profiles and models
  • Swarms
  • Mixture-of-Agents
  • Cron jobs

In multi-agent runs, child executions are nested within the trace, ensuring that a single connected trace represents the entire workflow. GPU and CPU utilization are monitored using host metrics.

#OpenTelemetry #AIAgents #HermesAgent #Observability #LLMOps

Source: briancaffey/hermes-otel

item.title: Dunetrace introduces deterministic runtime monitoring for AI agents
item.description:
Dunetrace introduces deterministic runtime monitoring for AI agents

Dunetrace has introduced a runtime reliability layer designed specifically for AI agents. The tool addresses the issue of silent failures in agent systems, where APIs may return status code 200 and latency metrics appear normal, yet the underlying logic is broken. Unlike traditional tracers that answer “what happened?” after a failure is already known, Dunetrace answers “is something breaking right now?” using deterministic checks in the request path.

🧩 How it works

Dunetrace operates on the runtime path of AI agents, enabling it to block actions before they execute. It provides the following core capabilities:

  • Structural and semantic detection: Identifying issues through code structure and meaning.
  • Runtime prevention: Stopping problematic actions before they complete.
  • Native root cause identification: Determining the origin of failures.
  • One-click fixes: Providing immediate resolutions for detected issues.

The system uses zero-LLM checks on every run, meaning it does not rely on language model calls for its monitoring logic. This ensures deterministic behavior. The tool tracks LLM calls, including streaming, and outbound HTTP calls without requiring changes at the call site.

⚙️ Key details

Dunetrace distinguishes between “exact runs” and “implicit runs” based on how the agent is integrated:

  • Exact runs: Supported out-of-the-box for FastAPI, Flask requests, LangGraph invoke, CrewAI kickoff, and Vercel AI SDK wrappers.
  • Implicit runs: If specific entry points are not wrapped, Dunetrace records LLM calls as implicit runs. However, these runs remain in “shadow” mode, meaning their signals are held but no alerts are generated because the boundaries of the run are guessed.

The primary data structure consists of Sessions & Events, which log every run, tool call, and LLM exchange. This raw data serves as the foundation for all other monitoring features.

🚀 Availability and Setup

Dunetrace is available for local development and deployment with the following requirements:

  • System Requirements: Docker, plus either Python 3.11+ or Node.js 22+.
  • Local Startup: The service runs on localhost with authentication disabled by default. The curl -s localhost:8001/ready command should return {"status":"ok"}.
  • Integration: Users can start Dunetrace, observe it catching failures without API keys or LLM calls, and then add it to their own agent code.
  • Remote Setup: If the SDK runs on a different machine or container, users must set the DUNETRACE_ENDPOINT environment variable to the ingest URL.

💡 Why it matters

The primary value proposition of Dunetrace is shifting failure detection from post-mortem analysis to real-time prevention. By operating in the request path, it allows policies to block actions before execution, addressing the problem of silent failures that standard observability tools often miss because they only record what has already happened.

#AIagents #RuntimeMonitoring #DevTools #LLMOps #Debugging

Source: dunetrace/dunetrace

item.title: Netdata provides real-time distributed observability with per-second AI anomaly detection
item.description:
Netdata provides real-time distributed observability with per-second AI anomaly detection

Netdata is a full-stack observability platform that covers infrastructure, application performance, digital experience, network performance, databases, logs, and cloud environments. The system is distributed and real-time, with its Agents collecting, storing, and analyzing data where it is generated every second.

🔍 Overview

Netdata monitors multiple layers of technology, including:

  • Infrastructure
  • Application performance monitoring (OpenTelemetry traces, service maps, RED)
  • Digital experience (real user monitoring, synthetic monitoring)
  • Network performance monitoring (SNMP, topology, NetFlow/IPFIX/sFlow, traps, BGP)
  • Databases
  • Logs (monitoring and management)
  • Cloud
  • AI troubleshooting across all components

🧩 How it works

The architecture relies on data staying close to where it is created, stored in independent hubs placed where they make sense. Netdata Agents collect, store, and analyze data locally per second, applying machine learning anomaly detection on every metric. Netdata Parents and Netdata Cloud then combine these data points into a single view without centralizing the data itself. Because every piece of data gets its meaning at the time of collection, dashboards build themselves and ensure every chart is correct. Every metric is scored for anomalies every second, allowing clusters of anomalies to reveal hidden dependencies and show how problems cascade across systems, networks, and applications.

⚙️ Key details

  • Cost Engineering: Netdata collects everything every second and engineers the cost down to about 0.6 bytes per sample, making it unnecessary to choose what to watch.
  • Scalability: The platform scales to 100,000+ nodes.
  • Agent Accessibility: The Netdata Agent is open source.
  • Unification: Netdata Cloud unifies and correlates data from distributed hubs.
  • Proactive Identification: Anomaly detection can identify issues before they become outages and steer engineering responses.

#Netdata #Observability #Monitoring #AI #DistributedSystems

Source: netdata/netdata

item.title: Monte Carlo releases official toolkit for AI coding agents
item.description:
Monte Carlo releases official toolkit for AI coding agents

Monte Carlo has released an official toolkit designed for AI coding agents. The toolkit bundles skills and plugins that bring data observability directly into development workflows, supporting integrations with tools like Claude Code and Cursor.

🧩 How it works

The release functions as a single mc-agent-toolkit plugin that works across supported editors. It bundles multiple capabilities, with each feature acting as a skill that can be used standalone or as part of a larger system. Skills are grouped by their specific job, falling into two main categories:

  • Orchestrated workflows: Sequence individual skills into guided multi-step flows.
  • Atomic skills: Can be invoked directly by name.

⚙️ Key details

The toolkit includes a variety of skills focused on data health, incident response, and agent observability:

  • Asset Health: Generates single-table health reports covering freshness, active alerts, monitor coverage, and upstream issues, intended to be run before building on a table.
  • Incident Response: Orchestrates the full incident lifecycle from triage to root cause and remediation.
    • Automated Triage: Scores and prioritizes active alerts, running deep troubleshooting on high-signal ones.
    • Analyze Root Cause: Investigates incidents using lineage tracing, ETL checks, query analysis, and data profiling.
    • Remediation: Proposes and executes fixes for data-quality alerts, assessing blast radius before acting.
  • Troubleshoot Agent Traces: Investigates AI-agent alerts and traces by kicking off the trace troubleshooting agent and guiding manual investigation.
  • Proactive Monitoring: Sequences coverage analysis, gap identification, and monitor creation into a guided flow.
    • Monitoring Advisor: Identifies coverage gaps and creates monitors for warehouse tables or AI agents, emitting monitors-as-code YAML.
    • Manage MaC: Handles the creation, editing, validation, and import of Monitors-as-Code YAML files against published JSON Schemas.
    • Tune Monitor: Recommends changes to sensitivity, segments, and schedules to reduce alert noise.
  • Account Analytics: Answers questions about the user’s Monte Carlo account and helps build dashboards.
  • Prevent: Acts as an edit-lifecycle safety net for dbt/SQL, auto-activating via hooks to surface blast radius and monitor gaps before edits.
  • Generate Validation Notebook: Creates targeted SQL validation queries for dbt PRs or local repository changes.
  • Storage Cost Analysis: Identifies storage waste (such as unread or zombie tables) and verifies cleanup safety using lineage.
  • Performance Diagnosis: Diagnoses slow pipelines and expensive queries across Airflow, dbt, Databricks, and other platforms.
  • Push Ingestion: Generates collection scripts to push metadata, lineage, or query logs to Monte Carlo from any data source.
  • Connection Auth Rules: Builds JSON rules for Monte Carlo connection types using live connector schemas.
  • Instrument Agent: Instruments Python AI agents for observability by detecting libraries, installing the Monte Carlo OpenTelemetry SDK, and setting up tracing.
  • Onboarding: Connects warehouses or BI tools (Tableau, Looker, Power BI) to Monte Carlo via the REST API v2 tools, choosing or provisioning deployments and emitting Terraform or scripts.

🚀 Availability

Users operating coding agents can install the mc-agent-toolkit plugin, which is recommended by Monte Carlo to bundle all skills, hooks, and related features. For those using Claude.ai (web or desktop) instead of a coding agent, Monte Carlo is available as a verified connector in the Claude directory, allowing direct installation.

#MonteCarlo #AIagents #DataObservability #ClaudeCode #DataEngineering

Source: monte-carlo-data/mc-agent-toolkit

item.title: Langfuse SDKs migrate to OpenTelemetry in latest releases
item.description:
Langfuse SDKs migrate to OpenTelemetry in latest releases

Langfuse has released new versions of its Python and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs, both rewritten to be built on OpenTelemetry (OTel). The legacy SDK clients are deprecated, and developers are advised to adopt the new instrumentation methods and use the Observations API v2 for querying traces.

🧩 How it Works

The new SDKs use OpenTelemetry to handle observability and tracing. For real-time data ingestion, the only supported path is OpenTelemetry, combined with the Observations API v2 and Metrics API v2.

  • Python: Use the langfuse package with get_client(), start_as_current_observation, or the @observe decorator. Spans are created using context managers and are automatically closed when exiting their blocks.
  • JavaScript/TypeScript: Use the @langfuse/tracing package with startActiveObservation or startObservation, along with LangfuseSpanProcessor from the @langfuse/otel package.

For offline evaluation, regression testing, and prompt management, both SDKs provide dedicated packages (langfuse for Python and @langfuse/client for JavaScript).

⚙️ Key Details

The legacy v2 and v3 client APIs are deprecated. Querying traces using legacy endpoints like GET /api/public/traces or api.traceList is no longer recommended; developers must use GET /api/public/v2/observations.

  • Data Freshness: All GET APIs other than the OpenTelemetry ingestion path can be up to 10 minutes behind.
  • Python Installation: Install via pip install langfuse.
  • JavaScript Installation: Install via npm install @langfuse/tracing @langfuse/otel "@opentelemetry/sdk-node@<0.300".
  • Version Requirements: The JS/TS SDK v6 requires Langfuse Cloud or self-hosted Langfuse v4.59.0 or later. OpenTelemetry JS SDK 2.x is supported; 3.x is not supported yet.

🚀 Availability

The new SDKs are available as the latest releases for both platforms, with JavaScript targeting Node.js 22+ for core tracing and OTEL helpers.

Package Platform / Environment Functionality
langfuse Python Observability/tracing, datasets & experiments, LLM-as-a-judge, prompt management, full REST API client
@langfuse/client Universal JS Langfuse API client for universal JavaScript environments
@langfuse/browser Browser Langfuse browser SDK for public-key score ingestion
@langfuse/tracing Node.js 22+ Langfuse instrumentation methods based on OpenTelemetry
@langfuse/otel Node.js 22+ Langfuse OpenTelemetry export helpers
@langfuse/openai Universal JS Langfuse integration for OpenAI SDK
@langfuse/langchain Universal JS Langfuse integration for LangChain
@langfuse/vercel-ai-sdk Universal JS Langfuse integration for AI SDK v7

#Langfuse #OpenTelemetry #Python #JavaScript #LLM

Source: langfuse/langfuse-python Source: langfuse/langfuse-js

item.title: OpenInference Traces AI Agents Using OpenTelemetry Standard
item.description:
OpenInference Traces AI Agents Using OpenTelemetry Standard

OpenInference is a specification that builds on OpenTelemetry to trace AI agents, including their LLM calls, tool use, retrieval, and reasoning steps. It defines how AI applications are recorded as OpenTelemetry traces, ensuring that instrumentation follows a consistent standard regardless of the framework or language used.

🔍 Overview

  • The specification defines which span kinds mark LLM calls, agents, tools, retrievers, and embeddings.
  • It specifies which attributes hold inputs, outputs, token counts, and metadata.
  • Instrumentation follows the specification so that traces read the same whichever framework or language produced them.

🧩 How it works

  • OpenInference builds on OpenTelemetry to capture the execution flow of AI agents.
  • Instrumentation libraries automatically trace popular model providers and agent frameworks.
  • The system records specific steps such as LLM calls, tool use, retrieval, and reasoning.

⚙️ Key details

  • Natively Supported Tools:
    • Arize Phoenix
    • Arize AX
  • Backend Compatibility: Works with any OpenTelemetry-compatible backend.

🚀 Availability

  • Instrumentation libraries are available for the following languages:
    • Python
    • JavaScript
    • Java
    • Go

#OpenInference #OpenTelemetry #AIObservability #LLM #AgentFrameworks

Source: Arize-ai/openinference

item.title: TruLens and BitRouter Enhance AI Agent Cost & Quality with OpenTelemetry
item.description:
TruLens and BitRouter Enhance AI Agent Cost & Quality with OpenTelemetry

TruLens and BitRouter, two open‑source tools, recently released updates that improve the reliability and cost‑efficiency of AI agents by leveraging OpenTelemetry observability and intelligent routing.

🔍 Overview

  • TruLens instrumentation built on OpenTelemetry.
  • BitRouter runs locally and exposes an OpenAI‑compatible API.

🧩 How it Works

  • TruLens instruments every function call, LLM generation, retrieval, and tool invocation as structured OTEL span.
  • Tracing is portable to any OTLP backend; export to Jaeger, Grafana Tempo, Datadog, New Relic, or any OTLP‑compatible backend.
  • BitRouter uses a Rust router between agents and model providers; routing policy lives in files you own; routes are inspectable and diffable; policy changes only when published; it learns from outcomes and proposes new policies.

⚙️ Key Details

  • TruLens records latency, inputs, outputs, tokens, cost per step; provides scores, latency, cost per app version; cheapest version often not worst.
  • TruLens judges graded against human annotations; 95% Agent errors caught with Agent GPA on TRAIL/GAIA; 267/281 human‑annotated errors vs 55% baseline trace judge.
  • Performance metrics: 0.81 Groundedness F1 on LLM‑AggreFact, 0.93 Context relevance NDCG@5, first of five tools on three of four ranking metrics, 4.2:1 context relevance adversarial win‑loss.
  • BitRouter cut API cost by 40.9% on Terminal‑Bench 2.1 while maintaining nearly same reward; dynamic routing between GPT‑5.6, Kimi K3, DeepSeek V4 Flash; savings due to routing decisions, not cheaper models.
  • Companies using TruLens: Walmart Global Tech, Cisco, J.P. Morgan Chase, Equinix, VMware by Broadcom, Hitachi Digital Services, Thomson Reuters, phData, HID Global.
  • BitRouter supports OpenAI Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, cross‑protocol routing; includes built‑in Codex and Claude support.

🚀 Availability

  • TruLens is open source and OpenTelemetry‑native.
  • BitRouter runs locally, provides an OpenAI‑compatible API; requires minimal changes; can be installed with npx skills add bitrouter/bitrouter; hosted routing presets use @<name>; local bitrouter/auto selector requires a local router.
  • Official macOS distributions support Apple Silicon (arm64) only; run bro for line‑based first‑run setup; native harness interfaces via bro claude, bro codex, bro launch <agent>.

💡 Why it Matters

  • TruLens enables tracing of every agent step, making errors traceable and providing clear cost‑quality trade‑offs.
  • BitRouter reduces API cost while maintaining performance by intelligent routing, demonstrating the value of routing decisions.

#OpenTelemetry #AIagents #CostOptimization #Observability #OpenSource

Source: truera/trulens Source: bitrouter/bitrouter

item.title: Parseable Observability Platform Integrated with Datasette via Codex
item.description:
Parseable Observability Platform Integrated with Datasette via Codex

On 6 October 2026 a new observability platform called Parseable was highlighted on Show HN.

🔍 Overview

  • Parseable is an observability platform with:
    • An open‑source implementation licensed under AGPL, written in Rust, packaged as a single ~180 MB binary.
    • An Enterprise version that adds extra features.
    • A cloud‑hosted option.

🧩 How it works

  • Datasette 1.0a41 added OpenTelemetry support.
  • Using Codex, the author figured out how to run Parseable and feed it traces generated by Datasette.
  • The resulting trace was displayed in the Parseable localhost web application.

⚙️ Key details

  • Open‑source binary: AGPL, Rust, ~180 MB.
  • Enterprise version: includes additional features (unspecified).
  • Cloud option: available as a hosted service.
  • Integration steps:
    • Enable OpenTelemetry in Datasette 1.0a41.
    • Use Codex to determine the commands needed to start Parseable and ingest the traces.
    • View the trace in Parseable’s web UI.

🚀 Availability

  • The open‑source binary and its documentation are publicly available as of 6 October 2026.
  • Enterprise and cloud offerings are announced alongside the open‑source release.

💡 Why it matters

  • The combination shows a practical workflow for connecting a data‑exploration tool (Datasette) with an observability platform (Parseable) using AI assistance (Codex).

#Parseable #Observability #OpenTelemetry #Datasette

Source: TIL: Using Parseable with Datasette for OpenTelemetry traces

item.title: NVIDIA NeMo Relay Integration for Hermes Agent Observability
item.description:
NVIDIA NeMo Relay Integration for Hermes Agent Observability

The Hermes Agent harness now includes native integration with NVIDIA NeMo Relay, allowing developers to record and evaluate agent sessions, turns, model calls, and tool calls.

🧩 How it works

NeMo Relay records lifecycle events as work begins and ends, preserving timing and parent-child relationships. This integration utilizes several formats and standards for observability:

Format/Standard Description
Agent Trajectory Observability Format (ATOF) A JSONL log of scope starts, ends, and point-in-time marks with IDs and timestamps to reconstruct the agent run.
Agent Trajectory Interchange Format (ATIF) A step-by-step JSON record of agent interactions, tool calls, and observations assembled from lifecycle events.
OpenTelemetry with OpenInference Records the run as parent-child spans, using OpenInference to label agent, LLM, and tool spans and define their attributes.

⚙️ Key details

Users can run Hermes Agent examples using a self-contained environment (Python 3.11, Hermes 0.21.1, and NeMo Relay 0.8.3) created via a setup script in the nemoclaw-community repository.

Capabilities and constraints include:

  • Terminal Tool Sandbox: Hermes uses a terminal tool to run Python scripts inside an isolated Docker container that cannot access the network, repository checkout, or NVIDIA API key.
  • Host Security: Hermes cannot fall back to running terminal commands on the host.
  • Observability Tools: Users can explore OpenTelemetry traces in Arize Phoenix.
  • Evaluation: The Hermes ToolPerf case study demonstrates using this approach to evaluate harness changes across repeated runs by combining task verification with trace evidence.

🚀 Availability

To get started, the following prerequisites are required:

  • macOS or Linux
  • Git and curl
  • Docker Desktop or Docker Engine
  • An NVIDIA Build API key for NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning

#NVIDIA #NeMoRelay #HermesAgent #OpenTelemetry #AIAgents

Source: Tracing Agent Harness Behavior with NVIDIA NeMo Relay | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: Traccia Launches OpenTelemetry-Native SDK for AI Agent Observability and Governance
item.description:
Traccia Launches OpenTelemetry-Native SDK for AI Agent Observability and Governance

Traccia has released a production-ready Python SDK designed for observing, evaluating, and enforcing policies on AI agents and LLM applications at runtime. Built on OpenTelemetry, the framework-agnostic SDK provides distributed tracing and governance for AI agents, agentic workflows, and multi-agent systems.

🔍 Overview

Traccia provides a set of tools to manage AI agents that can act, specifically controlling what those agents are allowed to do. The SDK is built for OpenAI Agents, LangGraph, CrewAI, and LLM applications in production.

⚙️ Key Details

Core Capabilities

  • LLM-Aware Tracing: Automatically tracks prompts, completions, latency, tokens, and costs.
  • Automatic Instrumentation: Auto-patches HTTP libraries, requests, and providers including Gemini (google-genai), Anthropic, and OpenAI.
  • Framework Integrations: Supports OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, and LangChain.
  • Prompt Management: Features load_prompt and prefetch_prompts with cache, fallback, and stale-while-revalidate. Prompts are fetched from the Traccia prompt registry by name and deploy label.
  • Evaluation: The evaluate() function runs scorers and tasks over a dataset to save experiments for comparison and promotion.

Governance and Security

Feature Description
@govern Runtime policy enforcement to deny or reshape tool/LLM calls using Loop Cap, Model Boundary, and Spend Cap
Guardrail Detection Passive detection of custom guardrails, provider-native safeguards, and AI safety controls
Security Controls Configurable data truncation and removal of secrets from logs
Compliance PII/PHI redaction helpers and evidence for HIPAA and EU AI Act transparency and integrity verification

Technical Specifications

  • Infrastructure: OTLP-compatible export to File, Console, SigNoz, Zipkin, Jaeger, and Grafana Tempo.
  • Metrics: Emits OTEL-compliant metrics for token and cost tracking independent of sampling.
  • Configuration: Uses Pydantic for type-safe configuration and a simple init() call for zero-configuration setup.
  • Performance: Includes async support, efficient batching, and low-overhead instrumentation.

🚀 Availability

Traccia is available on PyPI. Use of tracing and prompt fetching requires a Traccia platform workspace API key created under Settings $\rightarrow$ API Keys, defaulting to https://api.traccia.ai.

#OpenTelemetry #AIGovernance #LLMOps #Python #AIAgents

Source: traccia-ai/traccia-py
